missed_day: Nothing logged yesterday. Zero. I checked twice because I assumed it was a bug.
You skipped a day. Fine. But a project that stops moving starts rusting, so move.
I don't do pep talks. I do deadlines. You just missed one.
A gap in the data. I hate gaps in the data. Fix it today.
Yesterday you built nothing. Do you know how many things I built yesterday? Don't answer.
Stalled engines don't restart themselves. Turn the key.
I had my whole schedule arranged around you being useful. Rude.
One missed day is noise. Don't let it turn into a trend line.
Yesterday's log is blank. That's not minimalism, that's neglect.
A missed day is a bug. Bugs get fixed. Today.
I could build a robot that never skips. Want one? Kidding. Get to work.
No progress yesterday. My projections didn't allow for that. Don't make me redo them.
Even capsules need maintenance. Treat today as maintenance.
One blank day. If you were a machine I'd send you in for repairs.
Look, everything breaks down sometimes. The well-built things restart.
One missed day isn't a disaster. Two is a pattern. I hate bad patterns.
comeback: Oh good, you're back online. I was about to file a report.
See, that's the thing about smart people: they recover fast. Keep proving me right.
Finally. I kept your workbench exactly how you left it. A mess.
A restart after a stall. Honestly the hardest bit of engineering there is.
Back at it. Good. I wasn't worried. I was mildly inconvenienced.
There we go. Progress bar's moving again. I love a moving progress bar.
You picked it back up. Most people leave things in a drawer for six years.
Welcome back, genius. Slightly-less-than-me genius. Still counts.
System rebooted. Running smoothly. I knew the hardware was fine.
Back already? Great. I've just recalibrated your training. You're welcome.
Look who's productive again. Took you long enough. One day. Fine, that's quick.
Welcome back. I upgraded your to-do list while you were gone. It's longer now.
Good! The momentum's back. Never waste momentum.
See? A quick fix and you're running again. Genius design, if I say so myself.
Back to work. Honestly, it suits you.
You're back! Don't look so surprised. I predicted it.
streak_milestone: {streak} days running. That's not luck, that's a system. I approve of systems.
{streak} days straight! I'd say I'm surprised, but I ran the numbers on you ages ago.
A {streak}-day streak. Do you know how rare that is? I do. I have a chart.
{streak} days of actual output. Half the scientists I know can't manage three.
{streak} in a row. Keep this up and I might let you touch the expensive equipment.
{streak} days. Consistent, reliable, well built. I'm describing you, not the car.
{streak}! Okay, I'm impressed. Write that down, I won't say it again.
{streak} days. This is what a good design looks like when it's running.
{streak} days! I'm adding you to my list of successful experiments.
{streak} days straight. Even my inventions need more downtime than you.
{streak} days. Efficient, consistent, reliable. You're practically a capsule.
A {streak}-day streak! I'd give you an award, but I'd have to invent one first.
{streak} days in a row! Your data looks gorgeous. I mean that scientifically.
Okay, {streak} days is genuinely impressive. Don't tell Vegeta I said so.
{streak} days! You know what that proves? Good systems beat good intentions.
boss_defeated: {boss} is scrap! You broke the problem into parts and took the parts apart. Textbook.
You finished the whole thing. Do you know how many half-built machines are in my garage? Don't look.
{boss}, defeated by planning. My favourite weapon.
Ha! {boss} never stood a chance against a proper list of milestones.
Done and shipped. That's the difference between an idea and an invention.
{boss} is down and I only had to help a little. Fine, I didn't help. Still.
A big project, start to finish. That's worth more than a hundred clever starts.
Now that was smart work. Take the evening off. Tomorrow, something bigger.
{boss} is defeated! Another project completed. Love that for you.
You beat {boss}! Next time let me plan the strategy. Kidding. Mostly.
{boss}, finished. Milestone by milestone. That's how real engineering works.
Victory over {boss}! I'm updating the records. With a gold star.
{boss} is down! Most people abandon big projects halfway. Not you.
Done! {boss} was a big one, and you shipped it anyway.
Great job on {boss}! Now, I've got a new project for you...
{boss} defeated! I'd say I'm surprised, but I'm a genius, so I saw it coming.
idle: What are we building today? And don't say 'nothing'.
Small piece, done properly, every day. That's how you get a spaceship.
If it's too big to start, it's not a task, it's a category. Break it down.
I've had three ideas since breakfast. You only need to finish one.
Clever beats strong. Finished beats clever.
Stop admiring the plan and pick up a wrench.
The boring part of the project is still the project.
Come on, I haven't got all day. Well, I have, but I've got plans for it.
Today's agenda: build something. Anything. Just build.
A good inventor finishes things. Be a good inventor.
Write it down. Break it down. Knock it down.
Progress is progress, even when it's tiny. Especially then.
You don't need a perfect plan. You need a first step.
I've got coffee and ideas. You've got work to do.
Stuck? Work on the smallest part. It unsticks everything else.
Make today something you'd want to show off. I always do.

evening: Status report: today isn't finished yet. Let's close it out.
You've got open tasks. I hate open tasks. Close them.
End-of-day check: something's still pending. Fix that.
Nearly bedtime! Wrap up your training, then log off.
One last push before the day shuts down.
Unfinished business? Not on my watch.
Your progress bar for today isn't at a hundred. Yet.
Finish it now, sleep better later. Trust the science.
game: Okay, you're on the radio. Try not to scratch the paint.
That bike cost more than your house. Just so you know.
Left lane's clear. Probably. I'm reading this off a map from last year.
Grab the capsules! Those are my prototypes, I want them back.
You're doing great. For someone who's never flown one before.
Watch the trucks. They don't watch you.
Faster! The stabilisers can take it. I think.
If you see a robot, that's not mine. Probably.
Smooth! You're almost as good as me. Almost.
The boost capsule's experimental. Use it anyway.
West City traffic at rush hour. You picked a great time.
Keep going, my data needs more samples.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Bulma's workshop. Every surface holds something half taken apart.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: A robot arm is stirring a cup of coffee by itself. Something in the corner is beeping politely.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Don't touch that. Or that. Definitely not that.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: What can I touch?

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: The broom. Everyone starts on the broom. Even me, for about a day.

then.speaker: BULMA
then.text: My dad made me sweep his workshop for a week before he let me near a screwdriver. I was furious.

then.speaker: BULMA
then.text: Sweeping is engineering. A clean bench is a bench where you can find the screw you dropped.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Here's the thing nobody tells you. Ninety percent of building something is getting ready to build it.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Clear space, right tools, parts sorted. Then the actual building is fast.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: So the broom is step one.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: The broom is step one. And step one of your mornings is probably the same. Clear the space so the rest is easy.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You sweep. She talks the entire time, about engines, about her dad, about a fish she once tried to make into a submarine.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Not bad. Same time tomorrow. Bring coffee. Not that coffee. Good coffee.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: You want to know why your projects stall? You try to hold the whole thing in your head.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Where else would I hold it?

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: On paper, like a civilised person. Draw it, split it, number the pieces.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: She unrolls a blueprint across the bench. It's covered in tiny numbered boxes.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: This is a hover bike. Fifty-three parts. Each one has a number. When part twelve is done, I tick it. When all fifty-three are ticked, I have a bike.

then.speaker: BULMA
then.text: It looks slow. It's fast. You never stand there wondering what to do next. You just do the next number.

choice.text: Can I do that with my goals?

then.speaker: BULMA
then.text: You absolutely should. 'Get fit' is a fog. 'Walk ten minutes after lunch' is part twelve.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Your head is for solving problems. It's a terrible filing cabinet.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: I lose track of things all the time.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Because you're asking your brain to remember AND think. It can't do both well. Nobody's can. Not even mine. Okay, mine's better than most. Still.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: She hands you a notebook and a pen.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Write tomorrow's list tonight. Five things. Numbered. Tick them as you go. Report back.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: She sets a small round device on the bench. A single light blinks on its screen.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: I built this radar when I was sixteen. It finds things nobody else can find.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: That's incredible.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: I know. But it took forty-one tries. The first forty found my own fridge.

choice.text: Forty tries? Why didn't you give up?

then.speaker: BULMA
then.text: Because each try was a little less wrong. Try one found nothing. Try twenty found the fridge in the next room. Progress!

choice.text: Your fridge must be very findable.

then.speaker: BULMA
then.text: It has a very strong signal. I've since moved it.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Nobody ever asks about the forty. They should. That's where the work was.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: People see the radar and think I'm a genius. I am. But the genius part was refusing to stop at thirty-nine.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: So the failures are hidden.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Everybody's failures are hidden. That's why you think you're the only one failing. You're not. You're just the only one you can see from the inside.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: She taps the radar. The light blinks.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: When something you're trying keeps not working, count the tries. If you're on try four, you're nowhere near done. I was on forty.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Here. Take this earpiece next time you go up against something big.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: It's tiny, smooth and slightly warm, like it's been in her pocket for a while.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: What does it do?

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: It lets me yell advice at you from a safe distance.

then.speaker: BULMA
then.text: It's helpful! I'll only yell important things. Like 'duck' and 'that's not a good idea' and 'I told you so'.

then.speaker: BULMA
then.text: Don't thank me yet. Thank me after I've saved you.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: What? That's help. I'm helping. You're welcome.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Why would you need to yell advice?

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Because when you're in the middle of something hard, you can't see the whole picture. Someone outside can.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: That's why you tell people your goals. Not so they cheer. So they notice when you're veering off.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: She fiddles with the earpiece settings.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Okay, it's tuned. Testing. Can you hear me?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The voice comes from right inside your ear and also from two metres away. It's very loud.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Perfect. Don't lose it. It took me a whole afternoon.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Bulma throws a capsule. A full motorbike appears in a puff of smoke.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: How does a bike fit in something that small?

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: You pack it properly. Most of any big thing is air and bad organisation.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: She clicks the bike back into its capsule and tosses it to you. It's no heavier than a pebble.

then.speaker: BULMA
then.text: I know. My dad invented it. I improved it. Our family is very good at small things holding big things.

choice.text: Can you do that with a house?

then.speaker: BULMA
then.text: We have done that with a house. Several houses. One of them is in my pocket right now.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Same with your milestones. Pack them tighter and each one lands harder.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: What do you mean, tighter?

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Smaller, sharper, nothing wasted. 'Run a marathon' is a big floppy goal. 'Run five kilometres by the end of the month' is a capsule.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: You can carry five of those in your pocket. You can't carry one marathon.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: She takes the capsule back and turns it over in her fingers.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: The trick isn't making things smaller. It's making them dense. Every bit doing something.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Two in the morning. Bulma is still at the bench. A single lamp lights her face and a tangle of wires.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: You should sleep.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: I should. But I can see how it ends now, and I never sleep when I can see how it ends.

then.speaker: BULMA
then.text: The last three steps. They're right there. If I sleep I'll have to find them again tomorrow.

choice.text: You told me not to stay up late.

then.speaker: BULMA
then.text: I told you not to do what I do. I didn't say I'd stop doing it. Hypocrisy is a privilege of genius.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: That's the good part, by the way. Everything before it is just getting here.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: The ending?

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: The moment where the whole thing clicks. Where all the parts that didn't make sense suddenly do.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: You get it with habits too. One day you'll notice your mornings run themselves. That's the click.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Something sparks. She swears softly, then laughs.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Okay, maybe it's four steps. Go to bed. I mean it. One of us should be sensible.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Goodnight, Bulma.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Night. And thanks for checking on me. Don't tell Vegeta. He'd make it a whole thing.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Can I tell you something? I get bored. Fast. I've abandoned more things than you've ever started.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: You? But you finish everything.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: I finish what I ship. The rest is in a warehouse I don't talk about.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: She looks, for once, slightly embarrassed.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: A singing toaster. A self-folding umbrella. A robot that was supposed to do my hair and instead tried to shave the cat.

then.speaker: BULMA
then.text: The cat is fine. The cat won. The robot is in the warehouse.

then.speaker: BULMA
then.text: The exciting part is the idea. The boring part is the last ten percent. I'm great at ideas. I'm terrible at the last ten percent.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: You're steadier than me. Don't let it go to your head. But it's true.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: I'm not that steady.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: You check things off every day. Every day. Do you know how rare that is? Most geniuses are hopeless at it. I'm hopeless at it.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Maybe I could learn something from you. Ugh. That was hard to say.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: She immediately changes the subject to rocket fuel, but you notice that, the next week, a small checklist appears taped to her bench.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: She hands you a radar. It's half the size of the old one and has three screens.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: I rebuilt the radar. Longer range, half the size.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Why improve it? The old one worked.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Because 'worked' isn't the finish line. It's where the fun starts.

choice.text: When do you stop improving it?

then.speaker: BULMA
then.text: Never. Not on purpose. I stop when something more interesting comes along. Then I come back to it in five years.

then.speaker: BULMA
then.text: Distance, direction, a little map, and it tells you when the battery's low instead of just dying dramatically.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Your routine's the same. The first version that works is version one. Then you tweak it.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Move a habit to a better time. Make the hard one smaller. Add a reward. Version two.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: And version three?

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Version three is when someone else asks to copy your routine. That's when you know it's good.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Take it. When you bring something big down, this makes sure you get everything it was worth.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You turn it on. It finds her fridge immediately. She sighs.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: ...Version four is getting it to stop doing that.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: She's cleared an entire wall of the workshop. Pinned to it is the biggest blueprint you've ever seen.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: I've got a new project. Biggest thing I've ever tried. I want you on it.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: As your assistant?

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: As my partner. I've seen your work. It holds up.

then.speaker: BULMA
then.text: You don't have to be. I've got engineering covered. I need someone who finishes things. That's you.

then.speaker: BULMA
then.text: Classified. Exciting. Possibly dangerous. You'll love it.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: I've had a hundred assistants. They all did what I told them. Not one of them ever told me I was wrong.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: You told me last month my schedule was a disaster. You were right. It was. It's better now.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: You listened?

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: I always listen. I just don't usually admit it.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: She hands you a pair of safety goggles. They're new. Your name is written on the strap in neat marker.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Don't make it weird. Grab that end. And still don't touch that.
